t:
That the Secretary of War is hereby authorized in his discretion, and upon such terms and conditions as he may determine with or without monetary consideration, to transfer and convey all right, title, and interest of the United States in or to any historic military cemetery or burial plot located on military posts or reservations which have heretofore, or may hereafter, become abandoned or useless for military purposes, including the graves and monuments contained in such cemeteries or burial plots and approach roads and appurtenances thereto, together with the responsibility for the perpetual care and maintenance thereof, to any State, county, municipality, or proper agency thereof, in which or in the vicinity of which such cemetery or burial plot is located: 

Provided, That in the event the grantee shall cease or fail to care for and maintain the historic military cemetery or burial plot or the graves and monuments contained therein in a manner satisfactory to the Secretary of War, all such right, title, and interest transferred or conveyed by the United States, shall revert to the United States.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that State, county, and municipal governments are involved, so this is coordination with outside entities. However, they appear only as grantees of a property conveyance made at the Secretary of War's sole discretion and on terms he determines. The section requires no consultation, hearing, comment process, advisory body, or right to sue before the federal decision is made, so receiving property is not participating in the decision.
fable.s: to transfer and convey all right, title, and interest of the United States in or to any historic military cemetery or burial plot

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of War to transfer property to state or local governments. It does not require the Secretary to consult with these entities before making the decision; rather, it grants the Secretary discretion to determine the terms and conditions of the transfer. The involvement of state/local governments is as recipients of a grant/transfer, not as participants in the decision-making process via consultation or advisory roles.
qwen_block.s: That the Secretary of War is hereby authorized in his discretion, and upon such terms and conditions as he may determine with or without monetary consideration, to transfer and convey all right, title, and interest of the United States in or to any historic military cemetery or burial plot... to any State, county, municipality, or proper agency thereof

opus.w: The Secretary of War alone decides whether to convey historic military cemeteries, and on what terms. States and localities appear only as the ones who receive the property, not as parties consulted before the decision. The tempting reading treats naming state and local governments as coordination, but nothing requires or allows their input. Whether upkeep is satisfactory is judged only by the Secretary.
opus.s: the Secretary of War is hereby authorized in his discretion, and upon such terms and conditions as he may determine with or without monetary consideration, to transfer and convey all right, title, and interest of the United States in or to any historic military cemetery
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading and why it fails.** The section names outside parties: a "State, county, municipality, or proper agency thereof." It is tempting to treat that as consultation or coordination with local governments. It isn't. The Secretary of War decides alone and "in his discretion" whether to convey a cemetery, on terms he sets. The local government only receives the property and takes on its care. Whether upkeep is "satisfactory" is also judged by the Secretary alone. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue or object is created. Being on the receiving end of a federal property transfer is closer to receiving a benefit than to taking part in the decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of War to unilaterally transfer property to state or local governments. The decision is made solely by the Secretary ('in his discretion... as he may determine'), and the outside entities are recipients of the transfer, not participants in the decision-making process. This is a conveyance of assets, not a consultation or coordination requirement.
qwen_chat.s: That the Secretary of War is hereby authorized in his discretion, and upon such terms and conditions as he may determine with or without monetary consideration, to transfer and convey all right, title, and interest of the United States... to any State, county, municipality, or proper agency thereof
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that transferring property to a state or local government involves "coordination" or an "agreement" with an outside entity, thus constituting participation. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits, grants, or contracts, and this section describes a discretionary transfer of title (a conveyance) rather than a consultative process where the outside party helps shape a federal decision. The Secretary acts unilaterally ("in his discretion... as he may determine"), and the state/local entity is merely the recipient of the property, not a participant in the decision-making process.
